common_name: Enchanter's Spell Daylily (Annie T. Giles Award, Parent of Dragon's Eye)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or early fall in average, well-drained soil in full sun; divide congested clumps every three to four years to keep flowering vigorous.

directions: Registered by Elizabeth M. Hudson in 1982, Enchanter's Spell is a small-flowered diploid daylily bearing ivory blooms with a dark purple and chalky lavender eyezone above a lime-green throat, carried on compact 18-inch scapes. Semi-evergreen and reblooming through midseason, it won the American Hemerocallis Society's Annie T. Giles Award for best small-flowered daylily in 1991 and was later used, crossed with Janice Brown, as a parent of E.H. Salter's 1991 introduction Dragon's Eye. Plant divisions in average, well-drained soil in full sun, dividing congested clumps every three to four years to maintain vigorous flowering.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or early fall in average, well-drained soil in full sun; divide congested clumps every three to four years to keep flowering vigorous.

directions: Hybridized by E.R. Joiner and registered in 1988, Scatterbrain is a fragrant diploid daylily bearing light peach-pink double flowers with a light green throat, six inches across on well-branched, 32-inch scapes. It blooms and reblooms through midseason and went on to win the American Hemerocallis Society's Ida Munson Award for best double-flowered daylily in 2010. Plant divisions in average, well-drained soil in full sun, dividing congested clumps every three to four years to maintain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Firefly Frenzy Daylily (Ida Munson Award, Crispate Double)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or early fall in average, well-drained soil in full sun; divide congested clumps every three to four years to keep flowering vigorous.

directions: Registered by Jan Joiner in 2002, Firefly Frenzy is a very fragrant, evergreen diploid daylily with an unusual crispate, heavily double lemon-drop self flower above a light green throat, measuring about eight inches across on 30-inch scapes. Blooming and reblooming through midseason, it earned the American Hemerocallis Society's Ida Munson Award for best double-flowered daylily in 2011. Plant divisions in average, well-drained soil in full sun, dividing congested clumps every three to four years to maintain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Totally Awesome Daylily (Ida Munson Award, Pink-Rose Double)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or early fall in average, well-drained soil in full sun; divide congested clumps every three to four years to keep flowering vigorous.

directions: Hybridized by Sidney Glenn Ward and registered in 1993, Totally Awesome is a fragrant, evergreen diploid daylily bearing a pink-rose blend double flower with a yellow-green throat, opening in the early midseason. It later won the American Hemerocallis Society's Ida Munson Award for best double-flowered daylily in 2003. Plant divisions in average, well-drained soil in full sun, dividing congested clumps every three to four years to maintain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Peach Magnolia Daylily (Ida Munson Award, Peach Double)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or early fall in average, well-drained soil in full sun; divide congested clumps every three to four years to keep flowering vigorous.

directions: Registered by E.R. Joiner in 1986, Peach Magnolia is a daylily bearing a peach self double flower with a green throat, about five and a half inches across on 32-inch scapes, opening in the late midseason with reliable rebloom. It received an AHS Award of Merit in 1999 and the American Hemerocallis Society's Ida Munson Award for best double-flowered daylily in 2002. Plant divisions in average, well-drained soil in full sun, dividing congested clumps every three to four years to maintain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Peggy Jeffcoat Daylily (Ida Munson Award, Creamy Yellow Double)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or early fall in average, well-drained soil in full sun; divide congested clumps every three to four years to keep flowering vigorous.

directions: Registered by Jan Joiner in 1995 from a cross of Jean Swann and Rebecca Marie, Peggy Jeffcoat is a dormant diploid daylily with a pale, creamy-yellow double flower and a light green throat, ruffled and opening flat about six and a half inches across on 18-inch scapes. Blooming in the late midseason with dependable rebloom, it won the American Hemerocallis Society's Ida Munson Award for best double-flowered daylily in 2001. Plant divisions in average, well-drained soil in full sun, dividing congested clumps every three to four years to maintain vigorous flowering.

common_name: King Kahuna Daylily (Ida Munson Award, Clear Yellow Double)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or early fall in average, well-drained soil in full sun; divide congested clumps every three to four years to keep flowering vigorous.

directions: Hybridized by Clarence J. Crochet and registered in 1994, King Kahuna is a consistently double, clear medium-yellow self daylily with three oversized petaloids, measuring about six and a half inches across on 22-inch scapes and opening in the early midseason as a heavy bud-builder. It earned an AHS Award of Merit in 2001 and the American Hemerocallis Society's Ida Munson Award for best double-flowered daylily in 2000. Plant divisions in average, well-drained soil in full sun, dividing congested clumps every three to four years to maintain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Almond Puff Daylily (Ida Munson Award, Beige Double)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or early fall in average, well-drained soil in full sun; divide congested clumps every three to four years to keep flowering vigorous.

directions: Registered by Patrick Stamile in 1990, Almond Puff is a fragrant diploid daylily bearing a large beige self double flower with a green throat, about six and a half inches across on 23-inch scapes, opening in midseason. It shared the American Hemerocallis Society's Ida Munson Award for best double-flowered daylily in 1997 with 'Siloam Olin Frazier'. Plant divisions in average, well-drained soil in full sun, dividing congested clumps every three to four years to maintain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Vanilla Fluff Daylily (Ida Munson Award, Cream Double)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or early fall in average, well-drained soil in full sun; divide congested clumps every three to four years to keep flowering vigorous.

directions: Hybridized by E.R. Joiner and registered in 1988, Vanilla Fluff is a very fragrant, dormant diploid daylily with a pale cream to light-yellow double flower showing a deeper-hued halo above a green throat, about six inches across, opening in midseason. It won the American Hemerocallis Society's Ida Munson Award for best double-flowered daylily in 1996. Plant divisions in average, well-drained soil in full sun, dividing congested clumps every three to four years to maintain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Highland Lord Daylily (Ida Munson Award, Ruby-Red Double)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or early fall in average, well-drained soil in full sun; divide congested clumps every three to four years to keep flowering vigorous.

directions: Hybridized by R.W. Munson and registered in 1983, Highland Lord is a semi-evergreen tetraploid daylily bearing a gently ruffled, ruby-red double flower edged in yellow above a yellow throat, about five inches across on 22-inch scapes, opening in the mid-to-late season with rebloom. It won the American Hemerocallis Society's Ida Munson Award for best double-flowered daylily in 1991. Plant divisions in average, well-drained soil in full sun, dividing congested clumps every three to four years to maintain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Double Bourbon Daylily (Ida Munson Award, Amber-Orange Double)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or early fall in average, well-drained soil in full sun; divide congested clumps every three to four years to keep flowering vigorous.

directions: Hybridized by McEwen and registered in 1968, Double Bourbon is a dormant diploid daylily with ruffled double flowers blending rich amber, orange, and brown tones with yellow midribs, about four and a half inches across, opening in midseason with rebloom. It won the American Hemerocallis Society's Ida Munson Award for best double-flowered daylily in 1981. Plant divisions in average, well-drained soil in full sun, dividing congested clumps every three to four years to maintain vigorous flowering; this older dormant cultivar benefits from a sustained winter chill.

common_name: Double Cutie Daylily (Ida Munson Award, Chartreuse Double)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or early fall in average, well-drained soil in full sun; divide congested clumps every three to four years to keep flowering vigorous.

directions: Bred by Mrs. Edgar W. (Betty B.) Brown III and registered in 1972, Double Cutie is a compact, evergreen diploid daylily with lightly ruffled, soft chartreuse double flowers and a fresh green throat, about four inches across on scapes roughly 13 inches tall. It blooms early to midseason with an extended flowering period and reliable rebloom, and went on to win the American Hemerocallis Society's Ida Munson Award for best double-flowered daylily in 1975. Plant divisions in average, well-drained soil in full sun, dividing congested clumps every three to four years to maintain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Pojo Daylily (Ida Munson Award, Dark Yellow Double)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or early fall in average, well-drained soil in full sun; divide congested clumps every three to four years to keep flowering vigorous.

directions: Hybridized by Winniford and registered in 1972, Pojo is a semi-evergreen diploid daylily with small, consistently double dark-yellow self flowers about three inches across on narrow, grassy foliage and scapes around 19 inches tall. An early, heavy bloomer with good rebloom, it won the American Hemerocallis Society's Ida Munson Award for best double-flowered daylily in 1977. Plant divisions in average, well-drained soil in full sun, dividing congested clumps every three to four years to maintain vigorous flowering.
